samples.summary: A thread whose comment list is empty can never be deleted (permanent 404)
samples.evidence: `deleteThread`'s authorize callback does `this.assertCommentAuthor(map, threadId, rootCommentId(thread), author)`. `rootCommentId` returns `copyThread(thread).comments[0]?.id`, i.e. `undefined` for a thread with no comments. `assertCommentAuthor` then does `const comment = commentId ? findComment(...) : undefined; if (!comment) throw new NotFoundException('Comment not found')`. So a thread that exists in the map but carries an empty `comments` array — which `isThread()` happily accepts, since it only requires a numeric `length` — is undeletable through the API and reports 404 for a thread that `GET /comments` still lists. The same shape also makes `applyDeleteComment` unreachable for it. There is no repair path in the diff.

samples.summary: `applySlideChange` move can call `moveAfterByIndex(-1, from)` when `moveFront` is absent
samples.evidence: The branch is guarded only by `if (slides.moveAfterByIndex && slides.getElementByIndex)`. Inside it, the head case is handled by `if (to === 0 && slides.moveFront)`. An array-like that exposes `moveAfterByIndex`/`getElementByIndex` but not `moveFront` (the interface declares all three optional) falls through to `slides.moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` with `to === 0`, i.e. index `-1`, which is not a valid CRDT index and will either throw or move the slide to the wrong place — while the function still reports `to + 1 === 1` as the landing position. The plain-array fallback path is skipped entirely for such an object.

samples.summary: An unknown `layoutId` silently produces a slide built from the first built-in layout instead of a 400
samples.evidence: `addSlide` passes `layoutId` straight to `MemSlidesStore.addSlide`, whose `resolveLayout` is `this.doc.layouts.find(l => l.id === layoutId) ?? getLayout(layoutId)` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:173), and `getLayout` is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:197). A typo'd or stale `--layout` therefore returns HTTP 200 for a slide built from an entirely different layout, and the response (`{id, index, slideCount}`) does not report which layout was actually used, so the caller cannot detect it. The `layouts` catalog route added alongside does not validate the id.

samples.summary: Slide writes attach without an `initialRoot`, so a never-opened deck gets slides seeded with no master/theme styling
samples.evidence: `apply()` passes only `{ docKeyPrefix: SLIDES_KEY_PREFIX }` — no `initialRoot` — while every other write path in this change seeds one (`initialSpreadsheetDocument()`, `initialBoardRoot()`, `{ comments: {} }`). For a slides document created through the API and never opened in the editor the Yorkie root is empty, so `readSlidesRoot` returns `themes: []` and `masters: []`; `MemSlidesStore.addSlide` then resolves `master`/`theme` to `undefined` (memory.ts:181-186) and skips the `seedPlaceholderBlocks` styling branch entirely, so every placeholder is created without the master's fontSize/family/color. `doc.update` also writes a root holding only `slides`, which `ensureSlidesRoot` later has to backfill.

samples.summary: `mutateMap` seeds `{ comments: {} }` into a word-processor Yorkie document that was never attached
samples.evidence: The non-sheet arm passes `initialRoot: { comments: {} }` for BOTH `pdf` and `doc`. Yorkie applies `initialRoot` at attach, before the callback runs, so a `PATCH/DELETE .../comments/...` against a `doc` document that has never been opened in the editor makes the Yorkie doc non-empty with only a `comments` key — and then 404s. The editor's later `client.attach(doc, { initialRoot: initialDocsRoot() })` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:352) is a no-op on a non-empty doc, so the document opens missing everything `initialDocsRoot()` would have seeded except what `ensureTree` (docs-view.tsx:59) happens to backfill. The `list` arm deliberately passes no `initialRoot`, which is the correct shape here too.

samples.summary: PDF region anchor is not checked for staying inside the page or having non-zero area
samples.evidence: `parsePdfAnchor` validates each of `x, y, w, h` independently as `0 <= v <= 1`, so `{x: 0.9, y: 0.9, w: 1, h: 1}` (a rectangle extending to 1.9 of the page) and `{w: 0, h: 0}` (a zero-area, unclickable anchor) are both accepted. `pageIndex` is likewise not bounded by the PDF's actual page count, so a thread can be anchored to a page that does not exist and will never be visible in the viewer while still being listed by `GET /comments`.

samples.summary: `listThreads` sorts on a possibly-undefined `createdAt`, producing NaN comparisons
samples.evidence: `isThread` only requires an object whose `comments` has a numeric `length`; it never checks `createdAt`. `copyThread` then sets `createdAt: fromYorkieMs(t.createdAt)`, and `fromYorkieMs` returns its argument unchanged when it is not a bigint — so `undefined` passes straight through. `out.sort((a, b) => a.createdAt - b.createdAt)` then compares with NaN, which makes the ordering of a legacy/partial thread arbitrary rather than "oldest first" as documented, and puts a `createdAt: undefined` into the JSON response.

finding.summary: New `POST tabs/:tabId/move` collides with (and shadows) the existing row/column axis-move route, breaking it
finding.evidence:
`ApiV1TabsController` is mounted at `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs` and the new handler is `@Post(':tabId/move')` (tabs.controller.ts:201) → path `.../documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId/move`.

`ApiV1WorksheetStructureController` is mounted at `api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/documents/:documentId/tabs/:tabId` with `@Post('move')` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:256) → the *identical* path.

In `api-v1.module.ts` the controllers array lists `ApiV1TabsController` (line 56) before `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController` (line 64). Express/Nest dispatch to the first registered matching route, so every `POST .../tabs/<tab>/move` now lands in `ApiV1TabsController.move`, which requires `body.index` to be a positive integer and otherwise throws `BadRequestException`. The axis-move endpoint (`{ axis, srcIndex, count, dstIndex }`) becomes unreachable and returns 400 for every request.

This is not hypothetical for callers: the CLI's own `moveAxis` posts to exactly the same URL — `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:978` `POST /documents/${docId}/tabs/${tabId}/move` — used by `sheets-structure.ts:224` (`sheets ... move` for rows/columns). So the new tab-move verb silently kills an existing, shipped row/column move capability (and the two CLI commands now target one endpoint with two incompatible bodies). One of the two paths must change (e.g. `tabs/:tabId/reorder` or `tabs/:tabId/move-tab`).

verdict.reason: The claimed route collision is not present. The new tab-move handler in tabs.controller.ts is declared `@Post(':tabId/reorder')` (line 207), not `@Post(':tabId/move')`; line 201 cited by the reviewer is inside a doc comment that explicitly documents avoiding `move` for exactly this reason. Combined with the controller prefix at line 34, the effective path is `.../tabs/:tabId/reorder`, which does not collide with `ApiV1WorksheetStructureController`'s `@Post('move')` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:253) under its `.../tabs/:tabId` prefix (line 63). Since the paths differ, controller registration order in api-v1.module.ts is irrelevant. The CLI confirms the split: `moveTab` posts to `/tabs/${tabId}/reorder` (http-client.ts:550) while `moveAxis` still posts to `/tabs/${tabId}/move` (http-client.ts:983), so the shipped row/column axis-move endpoint remains reachable and is not shadowed or 400'd.
